frontier.hypothesis: A second set of `idx` in the OUTER loop body - at a program point where the target really does write $s0 - denies the birthing lift at zero cost AND at zero register cost, closing the JD chassis.
frontier.mechanism: KD proves an out-of-inner-loop second set kills the lift for free (78 insns, loop top exact) and that its only cost is the register the value lands in. The target writes $s0 in exactly two places: `addu $s0,$s3,$a0` at 0x800645DC, in the outer-loop block immediately before .L800645E0, and the if-body sequence. If the 0x800645DC write is a SOURCE-LEVEL statement in the outer loop body rather than reorg.c's duplicate of the stolen loop-top insn, then an outer-loop `idx = i;` / `idx = i + j;` is a second set at a point where the target itself writes $s0. Session 3's H15 killed that shape only in the MAINTAINED-INDEX form, where the inner loop no longer recomputes idx and the entry copy constant-folds to `move $s0,$s3`; the untried shape KEEPS the inner-loop recomputation, so the outer assignment is redundant-but-live rather than the loop's only definition.
